assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: The sandbag filling fixture is upside down with its three pipes pointing upward.
assets.caption: Invert the fixture.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: One empty sandbag is pulled over each of the fixture's three upright pipes.
assets.caption: Put a sandbag on each pipe.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: The fixture has been turned right side up, with one empty bag hanging beneath each opening.
assets.caption: Turn the fixture right side up.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: Sand fills all three fixture openings to the top while the bags hang below.
assets.caption: Fill to the top with sand.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: Two gloved hands lift the fixture straight upward while three filled sandbags remain on the ground.
assets.caption: Lift the fixture and leave the sand in the bags.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: The fixture is set upside down with its pipes upright beside the filled bags, ready for another batch.
assets.caption: Reset the fixture for more sandbags.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: Four completed sandbags have been moved into a line away from the filling fixture.
assets.caption: Move completed sandbags away from the work area.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: Plan view: runoff approaches a house from the uphill side; a short angled sandbag line steers it toward an existing safe drainage path, leaving the doorway and exit clear.
assets.caption: Choose a short route to safe drainage.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: Top view shows overlapping bags with folded ends facing incoming runoff; section view shows a wider base under a staggered second layer.
assets.caption: Overlap and stagger bags.

assets.creator: Mark Hughes
assets.alt: Place sandbags parallel to running water to help prevent overtopping
assets.caption: Place sandbags parallel to running water to help prevent overtopping

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: A partly filled bag lies flat, with sand spread toward the closed end and an empty tail remaining at the opening.
assets.caption: Flatten the sand toward the closed end.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: The bag opening folds underneath the filled portion, leaving a flat bag without a tied neck.
assets.caption: Fold the empty end underneath.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: Filled sandbags are stacked low on a pallet with offset joints, clear of the ground.
assets.caption: Stack low on stable support.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: Plan view of a house: uphill runoff meets a low sandbag line and follows arrows around the doorway and driveway toward an existing safe drainage path.
assets.caption: Plan the diversion before placing bags.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: Four flat bags overlap in a line, with each filled portion covering the previous bag’s folded empty end and water flowing along the row.
assets.caption: Top view — overlap adjoining bags.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: Three courses of bags have offset joints; the joints of the middle course cover the centers of the bags below.
assets.caption: Stagger each course by about half a bag.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: Cross-section of a low barrier with three bags at the base, two above, and one at the top; labels identify the water side and protected side.
assets.caption: Keep a wide, stepped base.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: A low angled line lies across part of a sloping driveway in front of a garage; an arrow follows the line toward a safe drainage path.
assets.caption: Driveway diversion toward safe drainage.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: A low sandbag diversion stands in front of a window well while the window and required access remain clear.
assets.caption: Low window well protection.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: Runoff follows a curved arrow around the free end of a sandbag line instead of reaching a safe outlet.
assets.caption: Water flowing around the ends.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: Labeled arrows pass through joints and underneath the sandbag barrier, showing that bags are not watertight.
assets.caption: Water seeping through the barrier.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: A curved sandbag line traps a pool on the building side; eroded ground beneath the end indicates possible undercutting.
assets.caption: Water pooling behind the barrier.

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: Wrong: bag joints line up vertically. Right: the upper bag bridges the joint below.
assets.caption: 1. Aligned vertical joints

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: Wrong: an overfilled rounded bag cannot settle tightly. Right: a partly filled bag lies flat and remains flexible.
assets.caption: 2. Overfilled bags

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: Wrong: four bags form a narrow column. Right: a low stepped stack has a broad stable base.
assets.caption: 3. Tall, narrow stacks

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: Wrong: separated bags leave a gap. Right: flattened bags overlap with empty ends folded underneath.
assets.caption: 4. Open gaps and loose ends

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: Wrong: a sandbag blocks a drain grate. Right: the drain is clear, with a labeled runoff arrow entering it.
assets.caption: 5. Blocking drainage

assets.creator: La Habra Heights Fire Watch handout contributors
assets.alt: Wrong: runoff arrows point toward a neighbor or road. Right: a low line steers water to an existing safe outlet on the property.
assets.caption: 6. Unsafe diversion

assets.creator: Mark Hughes
assets.alt: An overlapping sandbag line follows a runoff channel past a doorway.
assets.caption: Use staggered sandbags to guide water towards an outlet.  For stopping water, create a pyramidal berm.

assets.creator: Mark Hughes
assets.alt: A low barrier of overlapping sandbags extends across a doorway and beyond both sides.
assets.caption: Stagger sandbags in a square or semi-circular pattern around the door to keep mud and water out.

assets.creator: Mark Hughes
assets.alt: Sandbags stacked on a pallet
assets.caption: Sandbags should rotate 90-degrees at each layer to interleave like bricks with the bags below

assets.creator: Mark Hughes
assets.alt: A top down view of a home with sandbags directing water around it.
assets.caption: Use sandbags to redirect water to a safe outlet.  Do not dump your water into your neighbors lawn.

assets.creator: Mark Hughes
assets.alt: Four sandbags lying in a row.
assets.caption: Four sandbags lying in a row.

assets.creator: Mark Hughes
assets.alt: Sandbags stacked to form a stable base.
assets.caption: As you increase the height of a dyke, increase the width of the dyke as well.

assets.creator: Mark Hughes
assets.alt: Sandbags stacked near a basement window
assets.caption: Sandbags staggered around a basement window.

assets.creator: Mark Hughes
assets.alt: Use sandbags to divert water flow
assets.caption: Use sandbags to divert water flow along safe paths.  If it overtops the sandbags, give it a safe location for the water to flow.

assets.creator: Mark Hughes
assets.alt: Sandbags around a door.
assets.caption: If you place sandbags around a door, give yourself enough room to enter and exit.

assets.creator: Mark Hughes
assets.alt: Water burrowing in and underneath a sandbag wall.
assets.caption: Fast moving water is undermining a sandbag installation
